newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: MOODY'S ASSIGNS CZECH BANK ZIVNO BAA1 RATING.
newsitem.headline: MOODY'S ASSIGNS CZECH BANK ZIVNO BAA1 RATING.

text.p: Credit ratings agency Moody's on Thursday said it had assigned Czech Zivnostenska Banka a.s. a Baa1 rating for long-term foreign currency deposits and Prime-2 for short-term foreign currency deposits.
It added in a statement that for financial strength, Zivnostenska was awarded a D+ rating.

"According to Moody's, these ratings reflect the bank's significant position in teh Czech banking market, its focused strategy, its relatively good asset quality and its association with BHF-Bank as its largest shareholder," a Moody's statement said.
German-based BHF holds a 47 percent stake in Zivnostenska while the International Finance Corporation, part of the World Bank, holds a 10 percent stake.

The statement added that the transitional nature of the market in which the bank operates, and the fact that the bank "needs to grow its local deposit base as its local lending grows" were taken into account.

It said that "the likelihood that the bank's returns, which have been above average for the market, will be pressured by declining market spreads and by higher overhead costs as the bank expands its small branch network" was a factor in the ratings.
Zivnostenska's ratings are the same as those for sovereign Czech debt.
Zivnostenska is one of the 10 largest banks in the Czech Republic, with about two percent of market assets.
Unlike the other Czech banks hived off of the communist-era central bank in 1990, Zivnostenska has not been saddled with a large amount of classified loans.

BHF has also issued a comfort statement in its annual report that it will ensure that Zivnostenska is able to meet its liabilities, within the quota of its equity holding, except for political risks, the statement said.
Zivnostenska Banka had assets totalling 31 billion crowns at the end of the year.
